papers.title: Wastewater-based genomic surveillance uncovers broader SARS-CoV-2 diversity and spatial transmission dynamics in Georgia, January 2023-July 2024.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) using next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables real-time monitoring of circulating and emerging variants, often providing earlier detection than clinical reporting while capturing presymptomatic, asymptomatic, and symptomatic infections. However, the correlation between lineage abundance in wastewater and clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds in Georgia remains understudied. From January 2023 through July 2024, the Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) sequenced SARS-CoV-2 from 669 wastewater s
papers.summary: This study used next-generation sequencing of wastewater samples across Georgia from January 2023 to July 2024 to track SARS-CoV-2 variants, comparing lineage diversity in wastewater to clinical specimens from the same sewersheds. Wastewater surveillance captured broader viral diversity and provided earlier detection of emerging variants than clinical reporting, revealing spatial transmission dynamics across the state.

papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning and computational approaches can be used to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations and extensive intratumoral heterogeneity. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics are transforming the study of tumor evolution, while noting that resistance mechanisms remain poorly understood. The review synthesizes computational strategies for integrating these data to better predict treatment outcomes.

papers.title: DUET-seq: An Open-Source Droplet Platform for High-Fidelity Joint Chromatin and Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Temporal Regulatory Decoupling in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: Joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell enables direct linkage of regulatory elements to transcriptional output, but existing approaches remain limited by low co-capture sensitivity, proprietary platforms, and high costs. Here we present DUET-seq, an open-source droplet microfluidic platform for joint profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same nucleus. DUET-seq combines programmable dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads with one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to physically co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments, completin
papers.summary: DUET-seq is an open-source droplet microfluidic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and gene expression from the same single nucleus, using dissolvable dual-linker hydrogel beads and one-step intra-droplet RT-PCR to co-index RNA and transposed chromatin fragments. The platform achieves high co-capture sensitivity at lower cost than proprietary alternatives and reveals temporal decoupling between regulatory element accessibility and transcriptional output in single cells.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and medicinal-chemistry evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, making tumors more vulnerable to immune attack. The authors also discuss generative bioorganic frameworks as a design strategy for next-generation combination agents.

papers.title: Predicting Oncogenic Mutants of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Lung Cancer by Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a frequently mutated protein kinase found in patients suffering from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although therapeutic drugs targeting EGFR are available, not all patients respond to these drugs, and it is not yet known whether some clinically detected mutations are actionable. Although the oncogenicity of some mutants is well established, many mutants found in patients are not yet classified or classified as Variants of Uncertain Significance. For newly discovered rare mutants, strong evidence supporting their classification into oncogenic
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to predict whether EGFR mutations found in lung cancer patients are oncogenic. The approach aims to help classify variants of uncertain significance, which could guide treatment decisions for non-small cell lung cancer. The work addresses a clinical gap where many rare EGFR mutants lack clear actionability evidence.

papers.title: Machine Learning Guided Discovery of Microbiome Metabolites That Inhibit HDAC.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase (HDAC) is a family of key epigenetic regulator implicated in inflammation, metabolism, and cancer. Microbiome metabolites can modulate host histone acetylation, yet systematic identification of metabolites that target HDAC remains limited. Here we present a computationally driven discovery pipeline that combines training data composition optimization with experimental validation to prioritize microbiome-derived HDAC inhibitors. Starting from a large, public HDAC3 screening data set (314,129 compounds; 485 actives), we developed an automated iterative sampling strategy that
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning pipeline to screen microbiome-derived metabolites for their ability to inhibit histone deacetylase (HDAC), an epigenetic regulator linked to inflammation and cancer. Using a large public HDAC3 screening dataset, they optimized training data composition and prioritized candidate metabolites for experimental validation. This provides a computational framework for discovering microbiome metabolites with epigenetic-modulating activity.

papers.title: Gravlax: an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: A cell-by-gene count matrix is the artifact of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment that is most often stored, shared, and reanalyzed. It is the output of a computation whose inputs are the sequenced molecules and a gene annotation, and while the molecules never change, the annotation is revised continually. Once the matrix has been produced, the evidence behind it can no longer be reinterpreted. Recovering that evidence means returning to raw reads or alignments that are large, costly to process, and frequently unavailable. We ask whether a concise representation of the molecules themselves can b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Gravlax introduces an annotation-independent archive that stores molecular evidence from single-cell RNA-seq experiments, allowing the original data to be reinterpreted as gene annotations are updated. This avoids the need to reprocess raw reads or alignments, which are large and often unavailable. The approach preserves the underlying evidence behind cell-by-gene count matrices in a concise, reusable form.

papers.title: Functional Annotation of Alzheimer's Disease-Associated SNPs Based on Three-Dimensional Chromatin Structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have identified numerous loci associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the effector genes and regulatory mechanisms underlying many of these associations remain unresolved. This challenge is particularly pronounced for non-coding variants, whose regulatory effects may extend over long genomic distances and cannot be reliably inferred from the nearest gene alone. Here, we developed an integrative computational framework that incorporates three-dimensional chromatin interactions, expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL), and sequence-level regulatory
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates 3D chromatin interaction data, eQTL information, and sequence-level regulatory annotations to functionally annotate non-coding Alzheimer's disease-associated GWAS variants. By accounting for long-range regulatory contacts rather than relying on nearest-gene heuristics, the approach aims to link risk SNPs to their effector genes and regulatory mechanisms. This helps clarify how non-coding AD risk loci contribute to disease biology.

papers.title: Allele-Specific MicroRNA-Binding Variants at Colorectal Cancer Risk Loci in a Hispanic/Latino Population: An Integrative GWAS, All of Us, and Epigenomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) disproportionately affects Hispanic individuals, who remain underrepresented in genomic discovery and lack ancestry-matched functional resources. Many CRC risk variants are non-coding, and those in 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs) can alter microRNA (miRNA) binding sites and reprogram post-transcriptional gene regulation. Here, we identify allele-specific miRNA-binding variants at CRC risk loci within the Hispanic population using a discovery pipeline anchored to Hispanic-relevant resources. CRC-associated 3' UTR variants were compiled from the GWAS Catalog, further ve
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS data with the All of Us cohort and epigenomic resources to identify allele-specific microRNA-binding variants at colorectal cancer risk loci in Hispanic/Latino populations. The work addresses the underrepresentation of Hispanic individuals in genomic research by using ancestry-matched functional annotation to uncover non-coding regulatory mechanisms. It highlights how 3' UTR variants can alter miRNA binding and post-transcriptional gene regulation relevant to CRC risk.

papers.title: SMORE: joint dimension reduction and cell population discovery on single-cell methylome data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling technology captures novel epigenetic data modality but are challenging to analyze because of their heterogeneity, high dimensionality, and ultra-sparsity. Here we present SMORE (Single-cell MethylOme Reduction and Embedding), a computational method for joint dimensionality reduction and cell population discovery dedicated to single cell DNA methylation data. SMORE operates on a Bayesian framework that converts methylation proportions into ordered methylation states and jointly infers a low-dimensional representation, cell populations and their number. By u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMORE is a new computational method for analyzing single-cell DNA methylation data, which is notoriously sparse and high-dimensional. It uses a Bayesian framework to simultaneously reduce dimensionality and discover cell populations (including their number) by converting methylation proportions into ordered methylation states. This addresses a key bottleneck in the emerging field of single-cell epigenomics.

papers.title: HisTrader identifies nucleosome-free regions within ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications.
papers.abstract: Enhancers and promoters regulate cell identity through the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to specific DNA motifs within accessible chromatin. These regulatory regions are often identified using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based assays targeting histone modifications, such as ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq), HiChIP, and proximity-ligation-assisted ChIP-seq (PLAC-seq). However, the large size of the enriched regions, or peaks, can make it difficult to pinpoint the precise DNA sequence where TFs act or where trait- or disease-associated variants exert their effects. We present HisTrad
papers.summary: HisTrader is a computational method that identifies nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) directly from ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications, such as ChIP-seq, HiChIP, and PLAC-seq. By pinpointing these accessible regions within broader histone modification peaks, it enables more precise localization of transcription factor binding sites and trait- or disease-associated variants.

papers.title: Using Brain Organoids to Explore Human Neurobiology.
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in neuroscience is understanding how the human brain develops into a highly organized and functionally integrated organ, because many developmental processes cannot be investigated directly in humans and are not fully recapitulated in animal models. Brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells have emerged as powerful three-dimensional (3D) experimental models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, including regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. Recent advances in long-term organoid culture, organ
papers.summary: This review discusses how brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells serve as 3D models that recapitulate key aspects of human neurodevelopment, such as regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. It highlights recent advances in long-term organoid culture that enable the study of developmental processes difficult to investigate directly in humans or animal models.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Analysis and Experimental Validation Uncover Neddylation-Associated Biomarkers and Cellular Landscape in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that neddylation contributes to tumor initiation and progression. Nonetheless, its biological functions and regulatory mechanisms in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to identify neddylation-associated biomarkers and characterize the cellular landscape in lung adenocarcinoma. The authors link neddylation pathway components to LUAD progression and propose candidate biomarkers, providing new insights into the role of this post-translational modification in lung cancer.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers used to diagnose and classify central nervous system tumors, highlighting the shift from purely histology-based diagnosis to an integrated molecular framework. It emphasizes DNA methylation profiling as a key tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, alongside other genomic biomarkers with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Transcriptome-based epigenetic screening identifies DNA hypermethylation signatures as prognostic biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Promoter DNA hypermethylation is a key epigenetic mechanism of gene silencing in cancer, yet the DNA hypermethylome of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and its prognostic relevance remain poorly characterized. Here, we systematically identified and validated novel hypermethylated genes with prognostic significance in OSCC using a genome-wide discovery and multi-platform validation strategy. Candidate genes were first identified by pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing across OSCC cell lines, then validated by quantitative RT-PCR, methylation-specific PCR, and bisulfite se
papers.summary: This study used pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing to identify genes silenced by promoter DNA hypermethylation in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), then validated candidates across multiple platforms. The resulting hypermethylation signatures showed prognostic value, suggesting these epigenetic markers could help predict patient outcomes in OSCC.

papers.title: Phage Genomics and Bioinformatics in Therapeutic Development: Evidence Limits, Validation Gates, and Translational Decision-Making.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance has renewed interest in live therapeutic phages, including engineered candidates and defined phage cocktails, as antibacterial strategies. However, clinical translation requires evidence extending beyond phage isolation and computational prediction. This review examines how phage genomics and bioinformatics can support phage-based antibacterial development while remaining aligned with pharmaceutical requirements for safety, quality, pharmacology, and clinical validation. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes the literature on the generation,
papers.summary: This review examines how phage genomics and bioinformatics can support the development of phage-based antibacterial therapies, emphasizing that computational predictions and phage isolation alone are insufficient for clinical translation. It outlines the evidence limits, validation gates, and pharmaceutical requirements—such as safety, quality, pharmacology, and clinical validation—needed to advance therapeutic phages.

papers.title: The Plant Cell Wall: From Structural Diversity and Biosynthesis to Integrity Signaling and Physiological Functions.
papers.abstract: Plant cell walls are dynamic structural matrices that provide mechanical support while regulating growth, transport, environmental sensing, and defense. Their properties emerge from the coordinated biosynthesis, deposition, assembly, and remodeling of cellulose, hemicelluloses, pectins, lignin, and specialized wall polymers, yet how wall architecture is coupled to integrity surveillance and whole-plant physiology remains incompletely understood. Here, we synthesize current knowledge of plant cell wall classification, major polymer biosynthesis and assembly, cell wall integrity signaling, and p
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on plant cell wall composition, biosynthesis, and assembly, covering cellulose, hemicelluloses, pectins, lignin, and specialized polymers. It also examines cell wall integrity signaling and how wall architecture connects to whole-plant physiology, highlighting gaps in understanding these coupling mechanisms.

papers.title: The Epigenetic Aging-Cancer Continuum: Biomarkers, Metabolism, and Therapy.
papers.abstract: Aging and cancer form a biological continuum influenced by epigenomic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, cellular senescence, and loss of tissue homeostasis. Age-related epigenetic alterations can promote cancer, which exploits plasticity for evolution, immune evasion, metastasis, and resistance. Nutrition and metabolism affect this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl-donor availability, acetyl-CoA and NAD+ balance, redox status, microbiome metabolites, and chromatin enzyme activity. Circulating biomarkers such as cell-free DNA methylation, mutation-based ctDNA, fragmentom
papers.summary: This review argues that aging and cancer exist on a biological continuum driven by epigenetic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and cellular senescence. It highlights how nutrition and metabolism influence this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl donors, acetyl-CoA/NAD+ balance, and microbiome metabolites, and discusses circulating biomarkers like cell-free DNA methylation and ctDNA for tracking it.

papers.title: Flow Orchestrated Regulatory Genomics Engine (FORGE): A Configurable Nextflow Pipeline for End-to-End snMultiome Analysis.
papers.abstract: Single-nucleus resolution multiome (snMultiome) assays concurrently profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same nucleus. Yet regulatory inference from such analyses are difficult to scale, audit, and reproduce; moreover, as a field, snMultiomics and its' toolset remains far from standardized. To address these challenges we developed FORGE, a configureable Nextflow workflow that carries paired data from raw counts and fragments through regulatory network inference with a comprehensive differential testing suite. Execution is containerized, tracks provenance, robust to interr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FORGE is a configurable Nextflow pipeline that automates end-to-end single-nucleus multiome analysis, taking paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility data from raw counts and fragments through regulatory network inference and differential testing. It addresses the lack of standardization in snMultiome workflows by providing a containerized, provenance-tracking, and reproducible solution.

papers.title: A comprehensive map of the bovine mobilome and their epigenetic regulation of mastitis.
papers.abstract: Retrotransposons are major components of mammalian genomes, yet their genome-wide annotation and epigenetic regulation in cattle remain incompletely characterized. Here, we present a comprehensive annotation and integrative epigenomic analysis of major retrotransposon classes in the bovine genome, with emphasis on DNA methylation patterns and their potential roles in subclinical mastitis. Using a multi-step de novo pipeline, we identified and classified long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs), short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs), and endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in the bovine refe
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive genome-wide annotation of retrotransposons (LINEs, SINEs, and ERVs) in the bovine genome using a de novo pipeline, and integrates this with epigenomic data to examine DNA methylation patterns. The authors link these mobile element annotations and their epigenetic regulation to subclinical mastitis, suggesting retrotransposons may play a role in this disease. The work expands the catalog of bovine repetitive elements and offers a resource for studying their epigenetic control in cattle health.

papers.title: The Exposome-Brain Axis: A Scoping Review of Biological Biomarkers in Environmental Neurotoxicity, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The escalating global burden of neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders is deeply intertwined with cumulative environmental toxicant exposure. To accurately capture the prodromal and subclinical impacts of this multi-chemical "pollutome", research is shifting from symptom-based assessments toward the use of objective, quantifiable biological indicators. Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, this scoping review systematically analyzed literature across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase databases without temporal restrictions. The final selection included 52 human observational s
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 52 human observational studies examining biological biomarkers that link cumulative environmental toxicant exposure (the 'exposome') to neurotoxicity, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. It argues that the field is shifting from symptom-based assessments toward objective, quantifiable biomarkers to capture early, subclinical effects of multi-chemical exposures on brain health.

papers.title: H3K27me3 Drives Constricted Migration-Induced 3D Genome Rewiring in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Repeated exposure of neoplastic cells to mechanical stresses during metastasis can drive stable morphological and physiological changes. We previously showed that A375 human melanoma cells subjected to 10 rounds of constricted migration ("Bottom-10 cells") became significantly more migratory and exhibited H3K9me3 relocalization, transcriptional remodeling, and chromatin compartment changes relative to naïve parental A375 cells. Because these phenotypes persist across cell divisions, we hypothesized they are driven and maintained by specific epigenetic mechanisms. We profiled candidate histone
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how repeated mechanical stress from constricted migration rewires the 3D genome of melanoma cells, focusing on the role of the histone mark H3K27me3. The authors find that H3K27me3 is a key driver of persistent epigenetic and transcriptional changes that make the cells more migratory, linking mechanical forces during metastasis to stable chromatin reorganization.

papers.title: Predicting Capsid Protein Binding Sites in Single-Stranded RNA Viruses Using Machine Learning from Local Geometric Features.
papers.abstract: Selective recognition of viral RNA by capsid proteins is essential for genome packaging during the assembly of single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) viruses. However, identification of capsid protein binding sites in the RNA genome remains challenging because current experimental techniques are labor-intensive and low-throughput, motivating the development of computational approaches. Here, we present a sequence-based framework that integrates RNA tertiary structural modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict capsid protein binding sites. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a computational framework that combines RNA tertiary structure modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict where capsid proteins bind on single-stranded RNA viral genomes. Using the Qβ bacteriophage as a test case, the authors aim to bypass labor-intensive experimental methods for identifying packaging signals. The approach could help map genome packaging determinants in ssRNA viruses more efficiently.

papers.title: Deep phenotyping of EHMT1 ankyrin repeat domain missense variants in Kleefstra syndrome by multi-tiered structural genomics analyses at atomic resolution.
papers.abstract: EHMT1 is a lysine methyltransferase that writes and reads histone methylation marks to repress transcription. Deleterious mutations in EHMT1 cause Kleefstra syndrome (KLEFS1; OMIM #610253), a congenital neurodevelopmental disorder. Many of these affect the ankyrin repeat (ANKR) domain, which recognizes histone H3 lysine-9 methylation and mediates interactions with other epigenetic regulators. However, the functional consequences of EHMT1 missense variants within the ANKR domain remain poorly characterized, as nearly 50% are currently classified as variants of unknown significance (VUS). To add
papers.summary: This study uses multi-tiered structural genomics analyses at atomic resolution to functionally characterize missense variants in the EHMT1 ankyrin repeat domain, which are linked to Kleefstra syndrome but often classified as variants of unknown significance. By deep phenotyping these variants, the work aims to clarify their molecular impact on histone methylation reading and epigenetic regulation, potentially improving variant classification.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Prioritization of Candidate Drug Targets in Tumors Using Spatial Multi-Omics.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is reflected in cell composition, molecular states, spatial distribution, and microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics can map in situ expression and cell states but cannot fully explain upstream regulation, while spatial epigenomics provides complementary evidence such as chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation. This review summarizes the applications of spatial multi-omics and deep learning in prioritizing candidate drug targets in tumors.
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics) can be combined with deep learning to identify and prioritize candidate drug targets in tumors. It highlights that spatial transcriptomics alone cannot fully capture upstream regulatory mechanisms, and that integrating spatial epigenomic data provides complementary evidence for target discovery.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological covariates from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: Synergistic role of molecular imaging and genomics in thyroid cancer management: from diagnosis to personalized treatment.
papers.abstract: The management of thyroid cancer has advanced through the integration of molecular imaging, genomic profiling, and bioinformatics, supporting precision oncology across diverse subtypes. Although radioiodine imaging and therapy remain standard for differentiated thyroid cancers, efficacy can be limited in refractory cases due to heterogeneous iodine uptake. Advances including dosimetry-guided radioiodine therapy, hybrid imaging modalities (SPECT/CT, PET/CT, PET/MRI), and novel radiotracers (FDG, NaF) may improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic decision-making, particularly for aggressive tu
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining molecular imaging (such as PET/CT, SPECT/CT, and novel radiotracers) with genomic profiling and bioinformatics can improve diagnosis and personalized treatment of thyroid cancer. It highlights that while radioiodine remains standard for differentiated thyroid cancers, integrating imaging and genomics may better guide therapy for aggressive or radioiodine-refractory cases.

papers.title: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The inactivation of tumour suppressor genes is a key step in cancer development, and is usually achieved by homozygous loss. In prostate cancer, however, large genomic regions are often hemizygously lost, which complicates the identification of putative tumour suppressors in these regions. Here, we develop Epi2Hit, an integrative computational method that leverages whole genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling and gene expression to identify biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes involving DNA methylation of promoter and enhancer regions of one allele and genomic loss of the other a
papers.summary: The authors developed Epi2Hit, a computational method that integrates whole-genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling, and gene expression data to detect biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes caused by DNA methylation of one allele combined with genomic loss of the other. Applying this to prostate cancer, they identified recurrent epigenetic inactivation events and nominated new putative tumour suppressor genes that would be missed by approaches focused only on homozygous deletion.

papers.title: Long read sequencing of retinal RNA improves killifish transcriptome annotation.
papers.abstract: The African Turquoise Killifish has recently emerged as a powerful model for aging and age-related disease research studies. However, molecular based investigations have been limited by preliminary genome and transcriptome builds with incomplete reference genome sequence, fragmented chromosome assembly, and missing gene annotations. These issues make primary (alignment and quantification) and secondary (Gene Ontology, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis, cross-species comparisons) analyses difficult to reliably implement and interpret. This study seeks to generate a complete retinal reference transcr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses long-read sequencing of retinal RNA to improve the transcriptome annotation of the African Turquoise Killifish, a model organism for aging research. The improved annotation addresses gaps in the existing genome and transcriptome builds, enabling more reliable primary and secondary analyses such as alignment, quantification, and cross-species comparisons.

papers.title: Predicting Endometriosis Status and Menstrual Cycle Phase Using DNA Methylation.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with pelvic pain, infertility, and delayed diagnosis. Growing evidence suggests that altered DNA methylation contributes to disease development and could serve as a biomarker for disease. We developed a leakage-safe machine learning pipeline to classify endometriosis case-control status and menstrual cycle phase using genome-wide DNA methylation data from eutopic endometrial tissue. The dataset consisted of 984 samples profiled using the Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC array, with measurements across approximately 759,000 CpG sites.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study developed a leakage-safe machine learning pipeline to classify endometriosis case-control status and menstrual cycle phase using genome-wide DNA methylation data from eutopic endometrial tissue. Using 984 samples profiled on the Illumina MethylationEPIC array across ~759,000 CpG sites, the work demonstrates that DNA methylation signatures can serve as biomarkers for both disease status and cycle phase.

papers.title: Cross-Scale Convergence in Epigenetic Gene Regulation: A Perspective on Functional Enrichment Analytics for Cancer.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation of gene expression is studied at three physical scales: micro: DNA sequence-level methylation/demethylation; meso: nucleosome occupancy and remodeling; and macro: chromosomal domain silencing by Polycomb complexes, heterochromatin, and topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries. The challenge to fully understand epigenetic gene regulation patterns is that these scales are not independent. Their influence overlaps and they share a recurring architectural theme across scales of a targeted molecular pattern followed by cooperative, feedback-driven, spatially bounded s
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that epigenetic gene regulation operates across three interconnected physical scales—DNA-level methylation, nucleosome occupancy, and higher-order chromosomal domains—and that these scales share a recurring architectural pattern of targeted molecular action followed by cooperative, feedback-driven, spatially bounded responses. The authors propose that functional enrichment analytics must account for this cross-scale convergence to properly interpret epigenetic data in cancer. It is a conceptual framework rather than a new experimental or computational method.

papers.title: GenoME: a MoE-based generative model for individualized, multimodal prediction and perturbation of genomic profiles.
papers.abstract: The non-coding genome operates through a complex, multiscale regulatory system where regulated gene expressions are closely associated with cell-type-specific histone modifications, transcription factor binding, and 3D conformation. Developing computational models that can integrate these patterns to predict and interpret the regulatory system remains challenging. Here, we present GenoME, a Mixture of Experts (MoE)-based generative model that uses DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals to predict a unified genomic profiles encompassing epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin
papers.summary: GenoME is a Mixture-of-Experts generative model that takes DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals as input to predict a unified multimodal genomic profile spanning epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin features. It aims to capture the multiscale regulatory system linking non-coding sequence to cell-type-specific gene expression, and also supports individualized prediction and in silico perturbation of genomic profiles.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review compares targeted (amplicon- and probe-based) and untargeted sequencing strategies for wastewater virome surveillance, highlighting their respective strengths and limitations. It emphasizes that targeted methods offer sensitive detection of known viruses but cannot identify novel pathogens, and it discusses common bioinformatic pitfalls in wastewater sequencing workflows.

papers.title: DeCTCF: Decoding CTCF binding sequences by leveraging predicted epigenomic features.
papers.abstract: CTCF is a key architectural protein with diverse roles in genome organization and gene regulation, yet how it achieves these roles in different contexts remains unclear. Pretrained sequence-based models such as Sei provide predicted epigenomic features that can be used in downstream analyses of regulatory elements. Here, we developed DeCTCF, an integrative computational framework that uses pretrained Sei predictions to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences by integrating CTCF ChIP-seq data from 118 human cell lines. By leveraging predicted epigenomic features from the Sei model, we grouped th
papers.summary: DeCTCF is a computational framework that uses the pretrained Sei model's predicted epigenomic features to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences across 118 human cell lines. By integrating these predictions with CTCF ChIP-seq data, it groups binding sites to reveal how CTCF achieves context-dependent regulatory roles. The work demonstrates how pretrained sequence models can be repurposed to decode the functional grammar of a key architectural protein.

papers.title: Protocol for detecting germline copy number variants from whole-exome sequencing using agent-assisted Snakemake workflows.
papers.abstract: Germline copy number variants (gCNVs) are vital for diagnosing rare monogenic disorders. Here, we present a containerized, agent-assisted Snakemake protocol for detecting, annotating, and visualizing gCNVs from short-read whole-exome sequencing data. We describe steps for constructing baseline models, executing CNV calling, annotating variant pathogenicity using public datasets, and rendering interactive visual reports. This automated workflow simplifies routine management and ensures cross-platform reproducibility through a unified interface.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a containerized, agent-assisted Snakemake workflow for detecting, annotating, and visualizing germline copy number variants (gCNVs) from short-read whole-exome sequencing data. It covers building baseline models, running CNV calling, annotating variant pathogenicity with public datasets, and generating interactive visual reports, with the goal of ensuring cross-platform reproducibility through a unified interface.

papers.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Phenotyping for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: Algorithm Development and Multicenter Validation Study.
papers.abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a common psychiatric disorder, with two-thirds of affected individuals reporting severe impairment. Despite its substantial burden and moderate heritability, the etiology of OCD remains poorly understood, and treatments are often suboptimal. Although recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified some risk loci, much of the genetic architecture of OCD remains undiscovered, underscoring the need for scalable approaches to identify large, well-defined patient cohorts.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates an electronic health record-based phenotyping algorithm to identify obsessive-compulsive disorder patients across multiple medical centers. The approach aims to enable scalable identification of large, well-defined OCD cohorts to support genetic and clinical research. Multicenter validation suggests the algorithm can reliably detect OCD cases from routine clinical data.

papers.title: Microbial community composition on polytetrafluoroethylene tape retrieved from implant screw channels: A cross-sectional high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing study.
papers.abstract: To identify the types of microorganisms colonizing the surface of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape used for sealing the central screw channel in implant prostheses and to evaluate their association with the duration of prosthetic functional loading.
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing to identify the microbial communities colonizing PTFE tape used to seal the central screw channel in implant prostheses, and examined whether community composition was associated with how long the prosthesis had been functionally loaded. The work characterizes a clinically relevant niche for microbial colonization in dental implant systems.

papers.title: Clinical Epigenomics in Rare Diseases: Interpreting DNA Methylation Episignatures.
papers.abstract: Epigenomic testing complements sequence-based analysis by detecting downstream changes in epigenomic state associated with genetic variation. Genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures are reproducible molecular phenotypes that can serve as biomarkers of specific Mendelian disorders, particularly those involving chromatin regulators, DNA methylation machinery, and transcriptional regulatory pathways.
papers.summary: This review discusses how genome-wide DNA methylation episignatures can serve as reproducible biomarkers for rare Mendelian disorders, especially those caused by mutations in chromatin regulators and DNA methylation machinery. It argues that epigenomic testing complements standard sequence-based diagnostics by capturing downstream functional consequences of genetic variation.

papers.title: EndoPRS-SS: Summary-statistic based incorporation of endophenotypes to improve risk prediction.
papers.abstract: Endophenotypes are critical biological markers with genetic links to disease progression. We previously developed endoPRS, a multi-trait polygenic risk score (PRS) method that leverages endophenotype data to improve disease risk prediction. However, endoPRS requires individual-level genotype-phenotype data for model fitting, restricting its broader use. To address this, we introduce endoPRS-SS, an extension which enables PRS inference using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics and LD reference panels. Through simulation and real data analysis, we demonstrate that endoPRS-SS
papers.summary: EndoPRS-SS extends the endoPRS multi-trait polygenic risk score method to work with GWAS summary statistics and LD reference panels, removing the need for individual-level genotype-phenotype data. This makes endophenotype-informed disease risk prediction broadly applicable to researchers who only have access to public summary statistics. Simulations and real data analyses show the approach improves risk prediction over standard PRS.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Structural Characterization of Secondary Metabolite Biosynthetic Gene Clusters in African Baobab (Adansonia digitata).
papers.abstract: Adansonia digitata L., known as the African Baobab, is renowned for its extraordinary longevity and its long-standing use in traditional African medicine. However, the genomic basis underlying its specialized secondary metabolism remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to computationally identify and characterize putative biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) within the publicly available A. digitata genome assembly (GenBank accession GCA_029448705.1) using an integrated bioinformatics pipeline. Ab initio gene structure prediction was performed with AUGUSTUS (Arabidopsis thaliana species mode
papers.summary: This study computationally scanned the publicly available African baobab genome to identify biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) responsible for secondary metabolite production, using an integrated pipeline including AUGUSTUS gene prediction. The work provides a first genome-wide catalog of putative BGCs in this long-lived medicinal tree, laying groundwork for understanding its specialized metabolism.

papers.title: Epigenetics in cancer: from mechanisms to precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Epigenetics encompasses heritable yet reversible changes in gene expression that occur without alterations to the underlying DNA sequence. Through coordinated regulation of DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization, epigenetic mechanisms shape chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs that govern cellular identity, plasticity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, disruption of the epigenetic landscape has emerged as a hallmark of tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Unlike gen
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how epigenetic mechanisms—DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and higher-order chromatin organization—are disrupted in cancer and drive tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. It highlights the reversible nature of these alterations as a rationale for epigenetic therapies and their integration into precision medicine approaches.

papers.title: Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images.
papers.abstract: The functional decline of the hematopoietic system during aging affects organismal function and contributes to reduced healthspan. Quantifying hematopoietic aging holds great scientific and clinical relevance. Alterations in chromatin architecture are a well-established hallmark of aging that encode rich and informative signatures of the aging process, yet they remain largely unexplored as quantitative markers. Here, we present an interpretable deep learning approach based on convolutional neural networks, ChromAgeNet, that learns changes in the spatial features of chromatin architecture upon
papers.summary: The authors developed ChromAgeNet, an interpretable convolutional neural network that predicts hematopoietic stem cell aging status from 3D chromatin architecture images. This demonstrates that spatial chromatin features encode quantitative aging signatures that can be captured by deep learning, offering a new marker for quantifying hematopoietic aging.

papers.title: Investigation of allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids reveals the association between siRNA-mediated de novo methylation and high expression in citrus genomes.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation plays a central role in the regulation of gene expression. In plants, methylation occurs in the CG, CHG, and CHH contexts, via distinct DNA methyltransferases including MET1, CMT3, and the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway via DRM2. In interspecific hybrids, these epigenetic mechanisms are confronted to a mixed small RNA population and two subgenomes harbouring specific methylation patterns, therefore generating unique expression profiles. The aim of this work was to understand these regulations by analysing gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNAs in a citrus
papers.summary: This study examines allele-specific expression in citrus hybrids, integrating gene expression, DNA methylation, and small RNA data to understand how epigenetic regulation differs between parental subgenomes. The authors find that siRNA-mediated de novo methylation is associated with high gene expression in citrus genomes, suggesting a non-canonical relationship between methylation and expression in hybrids.

papers.title: Pan-cancer prognostic value of TGFBR1: Bioinformatics and experimental validation with a focus on gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: TGF-β receptor 1 (TGFBR1) is a key component of TGF-β signaling and has been implicated in tumor progression. However, its expression patterns, prognostic relevance and associated molecular contexts vary among malignancies and remain incompletely characterized within a consistent pan-cancer framework. In the present study, TGFBR1 expression, clinicopathological associations, survival outcomes, immune and stromal infiltration, genomic features, co-expression profiles and transcriptional programs were systematically evaluated using The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), TCGA-Genotype-Tissue Expression
papers.summary: This study systematically analyzed TGFBR1 expression across multiple cancer types using TCGA data, examining its associations with clinicopathological features, survival, immune infiltration, and genomic alterations. The authors then experimentally validated their findings with a focus on gastric cancer, identifying TGFBR1 as a potential prognostic biomarker in this context.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study analyzed DNA methylation patterns in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis patients to identify differentially methylated regions linking environmental exposures to disease. The findings highlight involvement of Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks, offering insights into early MS pathogenesis due to the short interval between exposure and disease onset in children.

papers.title: Precision engineering of upstream open reading frames for translational regulation and crop improvement.
papers.abstract: Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) are pervasive cis-regulatory elements in the 5'untranslated regions (UTRs) of eukaryotic mRNAs that modulate translation of downstream main open reading frames (mORFs) by shaping ribosome scanning, initiation, and reinitiation. By operating downstream of transcription, uORFs enable fine-scale control of protein abundance, offering a distinctive regulatory layer for precise tuning of gene expression in plants. Recent advances in ribosome profiling, translation initiation-site mapping, peptidomics, computational annotation, and genome editing have expanded th
papers.summary: This review discusses how upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in the 5' untranslated regions of plant mRNAs act as cis-regulatory elements that fine-tune translation of downstream main genes. It highlights recent advances in ribosome profiling, translation initiation-site mapping, peptidomics, computational annotation, and genome editing that enable precise engineering of uORFs for translational control and crop improvement.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for interpreting phylogenetic tree patterns in interkingdom horizontal gene transfer.
papers.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT), the movement of genetic material between unrelated organisms, is widely recognized as an important driver of genome evolution in bacteria. In eukaryotes, however, the evolutionary impact of HGT remains debated. The identification of interkingdom HGT (iHGT) is especially challenging due to the lack of gold standard methods. While automated approaches for iHGT candidate detection exist, the interpretation of phylogenetic tree topologies into biologically meaningful evolutionary patterns has traditionally depended on expert manual inspection, a process that is subj
papers.summary: The authors present a machine learning framework designed to automatically interpret phylogenetic tree topologies that arise when detecting interkingdom horizontal gene transfer, replacing the traditional reliance on expert manual inspection. This addresses a key bottleneck in iHGT detection, where automated candidate identification exists but biological interpretation of tree patterns remains subjective and labor-intensive.

papers.title: ChoCallate: a computational pipeline for consensus germline variant calling in genomic sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Accurate germline variant calling in non-model and polyploid organisms remains challenging due to sequencing errors, genomic complexity, and caller-specific biases. Existing ensemble methods of variant calling are constrained by species-specific training, limited portability, or an inability to process multiple samples concurrently. To address these limitations we developed ChoCallate, a Nextflow-based pipeline for consensus germline variant calling. The pipeline integrates three species-independent callers, bcftools, FreeBayes, and Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) HaplotypeCaller, within a flex
papers.summary: ChoCallate is a Nextflow-based pipeline that combines three species-independent variant callers (bcftools, FreeBayes, and GATK HaplotypeCaller) to produce consensus germline variant calls. It is designed to handle non-model and polyploid organisms, addressing limitations of existing ensemble methods such as species-specific training and inability to process multiple samples concurrently.

papers.title: The causal integration ladder: a multilevel evidence framework for therapeutic target evaluation in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Cervical-cancer genomic studies nominate many altered genes, but the evidence needed to distinguish disease association from a causal, therapeutically tractable mechanism is rarely stated explicitly. We present the Causal Integration Ladder (CIL), an evidence-accounting framework that distinguishes Level I association, inherited Level II-G evidence, acquired Level II-S evidence, Level III computational and direct functional evidence, and Level IV translational validation, while treating viral etiology as an explicit context modifier. An exploratory TCGA-CESC screen (306 tumours, 3 normal sampl
papers.summary: The authors propose the Causal Integration Ladder (CIL), a framework that organizes evidence for therapeutic target evaluation in cervical cancer into hierarchical levels ranging from association to translational validation, with viral etiology treated as a context modifier. They apply it in an exploratory TCGA-CESC screen of 306 tumors to demonstrate how the framework distinguishes disease association from causal, therapeutically tractable mechanisms.

papers.title: Novel Strategy for Structural Variant Genotyping by Short-Read Genomic Sequencing From Restriction-Circles: Experimental and Bioinformatics Proof-of-Concept.
papers.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) comprise copy-number variants (e.g., deletions and duplications) and copy-neutral SV (e.g., perfect inversions). Short-read high-throughput DNA-sequencing is the established technology for small-variant calling in clinical genomics, whereas Oxford nanopore or PacBio long-read NGS technologies improve SV identification but remain challenging to implement in clinical settings. We developed and validated a novel experimental protocol and bioinformatics pipeline for SV genotyping from short-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of restriction-circles of DNA. The experimental
papers.summary: The authors developed a new experimental protocol and bioinformatics pipeline that uses short-read whole-genome sequencing of restriction-circle DNA to genotype structural variants, including copy-number variants and copy-neutral inversions. This proof-of-concept approach aims to enable SV detection on widely available short-read platforms, avoiding the cost and complexity of long-read technologies in clinical settings.

papers.title: TattleTail: A Rule-Based Tool for Identifying Canonical Pyocin-Encoding Gene Clusters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Tailocins are phage tail-like bacteriocins derived from prophages that have lost the ability to package viral genomes while retaining bactericidal activity against related bacterial strains. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, these elements are referred to as pyocins and contribute to ecological fitness and antimicrobial applications. Despite lacking essential phage components, pyocin-encoding gene clusters share substantial sequence homology with phage tail genes, creating a major challenge for genome annotation. Current prophage prediction tools, which rely on phage gene homology, can frequently mis
papers.summary: TattleTail is a rule-based bioinformatics tool designed to identify canonical pyocin-encoding gene clusters in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which are phage tail-like bacteriocins that are difficult to distinguish from prophages due to shared sequence homology. The tool addresses the misannotation problem caused by existing prophage prediction tools that rely on phage gene homology. It provides a targeted solution for accurately detecting these bactericidal elements, which have ecological and antimicrobial relevance.

papers.title: Knowledge Mapping of Human Genetic Variation in Multiomics Biomarker Translation: A Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Human genetic variation and multiomics biomarker translation has emerged as a rapidly developing research field at the intersection of molecular medicine, bioinformatics, and clinical decision-making. This study used bibliometric methods to map its global structure, intellectual base, and thematic evolution. The eligibility framework was deliberately restricted to studies in which inherited or somatic human genetic variation was substantively linked to omics-integrated biomarker discovery, functional interpretation, clinical stratification, or therapeutic response; generic omics studies withou
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the research landscape linking human genetic variation to multiomics biomarker translation, identifying key intellectual bases, thematic trends, and global collaboration patterns. It provides a structured overview of how inherited and somatic variants are integrated with omics data for clinical stratification and therapeutic response. The study highlights the growing intersection of molecular medicine, bioinformatics, and clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Challenges in the detection and assembly of virus integration structures in human genomes.
papers.abstract: Oncogenic viral infections are major contributors to cancer development worldwide. Tumor-associated viruses such as human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) can promote malignant transformation through diverse mechanisms, including persistent viral gene expression, chronic inflammation, and, in some cases, integration of viral DNA into the host genome. Among these, HPV is one of the most clinically important DNA tumor viruses and is a major driver of cancers of the cervix, anus, penis, vagina, vulva, and oropharynx, col
papers.summary: This review examines the technical challenges of detecting and assembling viral integration structures—where tumor viruses like HPV, HBV, EBV, and MCPyV insert their DNA into the human genome—using current sequencing and computational methods. It highlights how these integration events contribute to cancer development and why their accurate detection remains difficult, likely due to repetitive viral and host sequences, structural complexity, and limitations of short-read approaches.

papers.title: Interpreting antimicrobial resistance from bacterial whole-genome sequencing: prediction tools, database fragmentation, analytical trade-offs, and harmonized reporting.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has become a critical component of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance because it can characterize bacterial lineages, resistance determinants, and, when sequence resolution is sufficient, the mobile genetic elements that mediate dissemination. However, the practical value of WGS-based AMR inference remains constrained by fragmentation across AMR databases, inconsistent nomenclature, variable curation practices, and differences in analytical thresholds and reporting rules. Consequently, the same isolate may yield discordant resistome outputs across tools,
papers.summary: This review examines how whole-genome sequencing is used to infer antimicrobial resistance in bacteria, highlighting that results are often inconsistent across different prediction tools. The authors attribute this to fragmented AMR databases, inconsistent nomenclature, variable curation, and differing analytical thresholds, and they call for harmonized reporting standards.

papers.title: Extensively Drug-Resistant ST16 Klebsiella pneumoniae Co-Harboring bla KPC-2, bla OXA-181, and Chromosomal bla NDM-4: Genomic Features and Therapeutic Challenges.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) represents a major global public health threat due to its high-level antimicrobial resistance and limited therapeutic options. The emergence of CRKP isolates co-harboring multiple carbapenemase genes further complicates clinical management and infection control. This study aimed to characterize the antimicrobial resistance phenotype, complete genomic features, and carbapenemase gene environments of an extensively drug-resistant ST16 CRKP bloodstream isolate co-harboring class A, B, and D carbapenemases.
papers.summary: This study characterizes an extensively drug-resistant ST16 Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream isolate that simultaneously carries three different carbapenemase genes (blaKPC-2, blaOXA-181, and chromosomal blaNDM-4), representing a rare convergence of class A, B, and D resistance mechanisms in a single pathogen. The authors use phenotypic testing and complete genome sequencing to map the resistance gene environments, highlighting the therapeutic and infection-control challenges posed by such multi-carbapenemase strains.

papers.title: A methodological framework for real-world performance studies of clinical variant classification platforms at early organizational stages.
papers.abstract: Automated platforms that classify sequence variants under the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework are increasingly used in rare-disease genomics, yet methodology for characterizing their performance at an early organizational stage is underdeveloped. The two framings most common in the literature are poorly suited to this stage: single-source comparison treats one peer laboratory or curated set as ground truth, which is difficult to defend at evidence depths where qualified laboratories disagree 25%-35% of the time; and for
papers.summary: This paper proposes a methodological framework for evaluating automated ACMG/AMP variant classification platforms during early organizational development, when traditional single-source ground-truth comparisons are unreliable because expert laboratories disagree on 25-35% of variants. It argues that alternative evaluation designs are needed to characterize platform performance fairly at this stage.

papers.title: In silico transcriptomic analysis nominates TSPAN32 as a central node of SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming in intestinal epithelial cells.
papers.abstract: Microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) regulate intestinal epithelial homeostasis and immune tolerance. Yet, the specific host effector genes that mediate these responses remain poorly defined, limiting the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) analysis of transcriptomic data to identify host genes that respond to microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in intestinal epithelial cells. The authors nominate TSPAN32 as a central hub gene in the SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming network, suggesting it as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: From sequence to timescale: a frequency-domain control-theoretic framework linking ncRNA sequence composition to epigenetic regulatory timescales.
papers.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are central regulators of epigenomic states, orchestrating chromatin modifications, gene silencing, and nuclear architecture through recruitment of chromatin-modifying complexes. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) such as XIST, HOTAIR, and MALAT1 exemplify these regulatory roles. Despite their importance, quantitative computational frameworks for linking ncRNA sequence composition to temporal regulatory behaviour remain limited. We introduce a frequency-domain control theory framework modelling RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, extending a previously established s
papers.summary: The authors propose a frequency-domain control-theory framework that treats non-coding RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, aiming to connect sequence composition to the timescales of epigenetic regulation. This is a conceptual/modeling contribution that extends prior work, but the abstract provides no experimental validation or concrete predictions.
